# K700: exact all-direction exclusion despite two Gaussian endpoint norms

At one explicitly specified 701-bit ordinary target, the lower and upper first-label residuals are both sums of two squares, and both prescribed switch factors are present. Three genuine primitive second-label chords pass at the same target. Nevertheless **every** first direction misses the strict window. The smallest attainable \(q\) is more than \(93 S/(64K^2)\), already greater than the upper cutoff, even before filtering for primitivity. This is a finite obstruction to the chord-window mechanism, not a counterexample to A303656.

For the two first-label norms \(S,R=S+2D\), any first chord \((P,Q)\) produces a Gaussian integer \(Z=\overline P Q\) with norm \(SR\) and \(q=S+D-\Re Z\). The exact product factorization is \(2^6\) times nine distinct split primes. In the Gaussian integers this yields \(2^9\) conjugate choices up to four units. The verifier exhausts all 512 choices and uses \(\max(|\Re Z|,|\Im Z|)\) per choice to account for those units. This upper bounds \(\Re Z\) for all directions, including any solutions the narrower algorithm would omit.

The replay uses trial division and Pratt certificates for small end-of-chain primes, and [the elliptic Hasse criterion](https://algo.inria.fr/seminars/sem97-98/morain.html) for the large ones. Each curve row checks an invertible discriminant and constructs an affine point killed by a prime \(q>(N^{1/4}+1)^2\), remaining affine and nonidentity modulo every prime divisor. A composite \(N\) would have a prime factor at most \(\sqrt N\), contrary to Hasse. The iterative curve operations require modular inverses, so unsuccessful inversions cannot accept an invalid certificate. All certificate and coordinate data are literal integers. Use Python 3.8 or later and do not use \`-O\`.

def root(a,n):
    a%=n
    if a==0:return 0
    if pow(a,(n-1)//2,n)!=1:return None
    q=n-1;m=0
    while q%2==0:q//=2;m+=1
    z=next(z for z in range(2,1000) if pow(z,(n-1)//2,n)==n-1)
    c,x,b=pow(z,q,n),pow(a,(q+1)//2,n),pow(a,q,n)
    while b!=1:
        i=next(i for i in range(1,m) if pow(b,1<<i,n)==1)
        v=pow(c,1<<(m-i-1),n)
        x,c,m=x*v%n,v*v%n,i
        b=b*c%n
    assert x*x%n==a
    return x

def ec_add(P,Q,n,a):
    if P is None:return Q
    if Q is None:return P
    x,y=P;u,v=Q
    if x!=u: m=(v-y)*pow(u-x,-1,n)%n
    elif (v+y)%n==0:return None
    else:
        assert y==v
        m=(3*x*x+a)*pow(2*y,-1,n)%n
    z=(m*m-x-u)%n
    return z,(m*(x-z)-y)%n

def ec_mul(k,P,n,a):
    Q=None
    for b in bin(k)[2:]:
        Q=ec_add(Q,Q,n,a)
        if b=='1':Q=ec_add(Q,P,n,a)
    return Q

def curve(n,j,d):
    if j==0:return 0,d
    if j==1728:return d,0
    u=j*pow(1728-j,-1,n)%n
    return 3*u*d*d%n,2*u*d**3%n

def check(n,t,s,j,d,x):
    assert n>3 and s>0 and 0<=x<n
    q,rem=divmod(n+1-t,s)
    assert n>q>(isqrt(isqrt(n))+2)**2 and rem==0 and gcd(n,6)==1
    a,b=curve(n,j,d)
    assert gcd(4*a**3+27*b*b,n)==1
    y=root(x**3+a*x+b,n)
    assert y is not None and (y*y-x**3-a*x-b)%n==0
    Q=ec_mul(s,(x,y),n,a)
    assert Q is not None and ec_mul(q,Q,n,a) is None
    return q

chains,pratts=CHAINS,PRATTS
def pratt(n):
    assert n>=2
    if n<2**32:
        assert all(n%d for d in range(2,isqrt(n)+1))
        return
    a,qs,es=pratts[str(n)]
    assert len(qs)==len(es) and all(q>1 and e>0 for q,e in zip(qs,es))
    assert prod(q**e for q,e in zip(qs,es))==n-1 and pow(a,n-1,n)==1
    for q in qs:
        pratt(q)
        assert gcd(pow(a,(n-1)//q,n)-1,n)==1

def norm(z):return sum(x*x for x in z)
def mul(z,w):return z[0]*w[0]-z[1]*w[1],z[0]*w[1]+z[1]*w[0]
primes=list(map(norm,gs))
assert len(set(primes))==len(primes)==9 and all(p%4==1 for p in primes)
for p in primes[:6]:pratt(p)
assert len(chains)==3
for p,chain in zip(primes[6:],chains):
    for row in chain:p=check(p,*row)
    pratt(p)

L,K=7,700
A,B=9**L,25**L
H,D,J,E=27*A+5*B,9*A+2*B,3*A+125*B,A+50*B
c=(E-1)//2
U=c*c+(J-H)//2;V=U+D
n=J+2*(t*t+c*c)
S,R=n-H,n-H+2*D
assert 25**128<=n<=9**224 and gcd(S,D)==1 and t%128==2
assert S==2*prod(primes[:4])*primes[7]
assert R==32*prod(primes[4:7])*primes[8]
ms=(7920,7922,7924)
P0=prod(m*m+1 for m in ms)
F=[]
for W,r in ((U,523595),(V,523928)):
    s=c-64
    u,v=r*r+W-s*s,2*r*s
    q=u*u+v*v
    assert q%2 and gcd(u,v)==gcd(q,P0*D*E*U*V)==1
    assert (t*t+W)%q==0 and gcd((t*t+W)//q,q)==1
    assert 64*K*K*2*u*u<q<64*K*(K+1)*2*u*u
    F.append(q)
assert gcd(*F)==1 and F==[prod(primes[:4]),prod(primes[4:7])]
qs=set()
for m in ms:
    v,r=divmod(t+m*(c+1),m*m+1);assert r==0
    a,b=(m*m-1)*v-m*(c+1),2*m*v-c-1
    P,Q=(t-c,t+c),(a-b,a+b)
    x,y=Q[0]-P[0],Q[1]-P[1]
    q,h=(x*x+y*y)//2,x*P[1]-y*P[0]
    T=n-J
    assert 2**K<=T<2**(K+1) and norm(P)==T and norm(Q)==T+2*E
    assert x%2 and y%2 and gcd(x,y)==1 and h%2==0
    assert 2*q*T==(E-q)**2+h*h and 64*K*K*q<T<64*K*(K+1)*q
    qs.add(q)
assert len(qs)==3
Z=[(8,0)]
for a,b in gs:Z=[mul(z,w) for z in Z for w in ((a,b),(a,-b))]
assert len(set(Z))==512 and all(norm(z)==S*R for z in Z)
qmin=S+D-max(max(map(abs,z)) for z in Z)
assert 64*K*K*qmin>93*S
a,b=gs[0]
assert 32*b*b>a*a+b*b and 2*(a*a-b*b)**2>(a*a+b*b)**2
assert (primes[-2]*primes[-1]).bit_length()==1167 and primes[-2]*primes[-1]>R
print('K700: 9 proven primes, 3 second seeds, 2048 products, ratio > 93')
